content: Do not take lisinopril if you are pregnant. If you become pregnant while taking lisinopril, contact your doctor immediately, as this medication can harm the fetus. Lisinopril is prescribed to treat high blood pressure, either alone or in combination with other medications. It is also used in combination with other drugs to manage heart failure. Additionally, lisinopril is used to improve survival rates following a heart attack. This medication belongs to a class of drugs known as angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors. It works by reducing certain chemicals that constrict blood vessels, allowing blood to flow more smoothly and enabling the heart to pump blood more efficiently. Lisinopril is available as an oral tablet and is typically taken once daily. To ensure consistent use, take it at the same time every day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take lisinopril exactly as directed. Do not take more or less than prescribed, and do not take it more frequently than instructed by your doctor. Your doctor will likely start you on a low dose and gradually increase it. While lisinopril helps control high blood pressure and heart failure, it does not cure these conditions. Continue taking lisinopril even if you feel well, and do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before taking lisinopril, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to lisinopril or any other ACE inhibitors, such as enalapril, benazepril, captopril, fosinopril, moexipril, perindopril, quinapril, ramipril, or trandolapril. Also, inform them about all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Be sure to mention aspirin, NSAIDs (e.g., indomethacin), diuretics (water pills), lithium, and potassium supplements. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you closely for side effects. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had heart or kidney disease, diabetes, lupus, scleroderma, or angioedema (a condition causing difficulty swallowing or breathing and painful swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs). Let your doctor know if you plan to become pregnant or are breastfeeding. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking lisinopril. Be aware that diarrhea, vomiting, dehydration, or excessive sweating can lead to a drop in blood pressure, causing lightheadedness or fainting. Consult your doctor before using salt substitutes containing potassium. If your doctor prescribes a low-salt or low-sodium diet, follow these instructions carefully. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Lisinopril may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: cough, dizziness, headache, excessive tiredness, upset stomach, diarrhea, weakness, sneezing, runny nose, decreased sexual ability, or rash. Some side effects can be serious. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of the following: swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs; hoarseness; difficulty breathing or swallowing; fever, sore throat, chills, or other signs of infection; yellowing of the skin or eyes; lightheadedness; fainting; or chest pain. If you experience any unusual problems while taking this medication, contact your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store lisinopril in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly. Consult your pharmacist about the correct disposal method. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the victim has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911. Symptoms of overdose may include lightheadedness and fainting. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your blood pressure should be checked regularly to monitor your response to lisinopril. Your doctor may order lab tests to evaluate your body’s response to the medication. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
